title: Further discussion: the environment
examiner_prompt: Now, I'd like to ask you some more questions about the environment. Please answer in your own words.

conversation.speaker: examiner
conversation.text: Do you think people in your country care enough about the environment?

conversation.speaker: you
conversation.suggested: I think more and more people care about it, especially young people, but many still don't change their habits. For example, a lot of people continue to use their cars for short trips, even though there are other options.

conversation.speaker: examiner
conversation.text: And what about you? Do you agree?

conversation.speaker: partner
conversation.text: I agree to some extent. I think people care in theory, but in practice it's difficult because eco-friendly products are often more expensive. Governments should do more to help.

conversation.speaker: examiner
conversation.text: Who should be responsible for protecting the environment: individuals or governments?

conversation.speaker: partner
conversation.text: Personally, I think it's mainly the government's job, because they can make laws and invest in clean energy. But individuals can help too, by doing small things every day.

conversation.speaker: you
conversation.suggested: I think it's a shared responsibility. Governments should set the rules and provide solutions like public transport, but we also have to do our part, for instance by recycling and saving energy at home.

conversation.speaker: examiner
conversation.text: How could schools teach children to look after the planet?

conversation.speaker: you
conversation.suggested: Schools could organise activities such as planting trees or cleaning a beach. When children learn by doing, they remember it better, and they often teach their parents too.

conversation.speaker: partner
conversation.text: I agree. I would also add that teachers should give a good example, for instance by reducing paper and using less plastic in the classroom.

conversation.speaker: examiner
conversation.text: Thank you. That is the end of the test.

title: Further discussion: learning English
examiner_prompt: Now, I'd like to ask you some more questions about learning languages. Please answer in your own words.

conversation.speaker: examiner
conversation.text: Why do you think so many people want to learn English nowadays?

conversation.speaker: you
conversation.suggested: I think it's because English is the language of business, technology and travel. If you speak it well, you have more job opportunities and you can communicate with people from all over the world.

conversation.speaker: partner
conversation.text: I agree with that. Also, so much of the music, series and social media we enjoy is in English, so many people learn it simply because they find it fun and useful.

conversation.speaker: examiner
conversation.text: Is it better to learn a language in a classroom or on your own?

conversation.speaker: partner
conversation.text: I think a classroom is better for beginners, because a teacher can correct your mistakes and keep you motivated. However, it also depends on your schedule and your personality.

conversation.speaker: you
conversation.suggested: For me, the best option is a mix of both. In class you get feedback and structure, but on your own you can practise at your own pace, for example by watching videos or using apps.

conversation.speaker: examiner
conversation.text: Do you think children should start learning foreign languages at a very young age?

conversation.speaker: you
conversation.suggested: Yes, I do. Young children learn pronunciation more naturally, and they are not afraid of making mistakes. If they start early, speaking another language becomes normal for them.

conversation.speaker: partner
conversation.text: I think so too, as long as it's done through games and songs, not through long grammar lessons.

conversation.speaker: examiner
conversation.text: Thank you. That is the end of the test.
